# 2 Kings Chapter 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 240v–241v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_019_page_479.jpg, 2KI_019_page_480.jpg, 2KI_019_page_481.jpg

---

**1** When King Hezekiah heard the report, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the LORD's temple.

**2** He sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the court secretary, and the senior priests — all wearing sackcloth — to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

**3** They told him, "This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of anguish, punishment, and humiliation. We are like a woman in labor who has no strength left to deliver her child.

**4** Perhaps the LORD your God has heard every word the Rabshakeh spoke when his master the king of Assyria sent him to mock the living God — and perhaps the LORD your God will punish him for what he said. Please pray for the remnant that still survives."

**5** When Hezekiah's officials arrived,

**6** Isaiah told them, "Tell your master this is what the LORD says: Don't be afraid of the words you heard — the blasphemies the king of Assyria's underlings spoke against me.

**7** Listen: I am going to put a spirit in him so that when he hears a certain report, he will return to his own country. And there I will have him cut down by the sword."

**8** Meanwhile, the Rabshakeh withdrew and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, having heard that the king had moved from Lachish.

**9** Then Sennacherib received word that King Tirhakah of Cush was marching out to fight him. So he sent messengers back to Hezekiah with this message:

**10** "Tell Hezekiah king of Judah: Don't let the God you trust in fool you by promising that Jerusalem won't fall to the king of Assyria.

**11** You know perfectly well what the kings of Assyria have done to every other land — totally destroyed them. Do you really think you'll be the exception?

**12** Did the gods of those nations rescue them? My predecessors destroyed Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar.

**13** Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah now?"

**14** Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers, read it, then went up to the LORD's temple and spread it open before the LORD.

**15** He prayed: "O LORD, God of Israel, enthroned between the cherubim — you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.

**16** LORD, bend down and listen. LORD, open your eyes and see. Hear the words Sennacherib has sent to insult the living God.

**17** It is true, LORD — the kings of Assyria have devastated nation after nation, burning their lands.

**18** They threw their gods into the fire and destroyed them — but those were not real gods, just wood and stone shaped by human hands.

**19** Now, LORD our God, rescue us from Sennacherib's power so that every kingdom on earth will know that you alone, LORD, are God."

**20** Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I have heard your prayer about Sennacherib king of Assyria.

**21** And this is what the LORD has declared about him:

The virgin daughter of Zion
    despises you and laughs at you.
The daughter of Jerusalem
    shakes her head as you run away.

**22** Who is it you have mocked and insulted?
    Against whom have you raised your voice
    and lifted your arrogant eyes?
    Against the Holy One of Israel!

**23** Through your messengers
    you have heaped insults on the Lord.
You boasted, 'With my vast chariot force
    I have climbed the highest mountains,
    the remotest peaks of Lebanon.
I have cut down its tallest cedars,
    its finest cypress trees.
I have reached its farthest corners,
    its densest forests.

**24** I have dug wells in foreign lands and drunk their water.
    With the soles of my feet
    I have dried up all the rivers of Egypt.'

**25** But have you not heard?
    I determined this long ago.
    I planned it in ancient times.
Now I have brought it about —
    that you should crush fortified cities
    into heaps of rubble.

**26** Their people, drained of power,
    were terrified and ashamed.
They were like grass in the field,
    like tender green plants,
like grass sprouting on a rooftop,
    scorched before it can grow.

**27** But I know everything about you —
    when you sit, when you leave, when you return,
    and how you rage against me.

**28** Because of your raging against me
    and your arrogance that has reached my ears,
I will put my hook in your nose
    and my bit in your mouth,
and I will drag you back
    the same way you came.

**29** "And this will be your sign, Hezekiah: this year you will eat only what grows on its own. Next year, the same. But in the third year, plant and harvest, tend vineyards and eat their fruit.

**30** The surviving remnant of Judah will be like a tree that sends roots deep into the ground and bears fruit above.

**31** For a remnant will emerge from Jerusalem, a group of survivors from Mount Zion. The passionate commitment of the LORD of Armies will make this happen.

**32** "So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city. He will not shoot a single arrow here. He will not advance against it with shields. He will not build a siege ramp against it.

**33** He will go home the same way he came. He will not enter this city, declares the LORD.

**34** I will defend this city and save it — for my own honor and for the sake of my servant David."

**35** That very night, the angel of the LORD went out to the Assyrian camp and struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand soldiers. When the surviving Assyrians woke at dawn, they found the camp filled with corpses.

**36** So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp, withdrew, and returned to Nineveh.

**37** One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, two of his own sons — Adrammelech and Sharezer — assassinated him with their swords and fled to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon succeeded him as king.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 3 — "a woman in labor with no strength":** Hezekiah's metaphor is visceral and desperate. The nation is at the crisis point — the moment when everything depends on the next push — but the strength is gone. It captures the feeling of being caught between catastrophe and deliverance with no ability to determine the outcome.

**Verse 14 — Spreading the letter:** This is one of the most remarkable prayer scenes in the Bible. Hezekiah does not summarize Sennacherib's threats — he literally opens the letter and lays it before God, as if saying, "Read this yourself." It is prayer as evidence presentation, trust as a physical gesture.

**Verse 21 — Virgin daughter Zion:** The poetry is breathtaking in its audacity. Jerusalem — besieged, threatened, facing the most powerful army on earth — is personified as an untouched young woman who laughs contemptuously at Sennacherib as he retreats. She shakes her head behind him. The reversal is total: the predator becomes the joke.

**Verse 25 — "I determined this long ago":** This is the chapter's theological pivot. Sennacherib boasted of his conquests. YHWH's response: "Those were my conquests, not yours. I planned them before you existed. You were the tool, not the craftsman." It demolishes every imperial claim to self-made greatness.

**Verse 28 — "hook in your nose":** The imagery is drawn from the Assyrians' own practice of leading captive kings by nose-rings. YHWH turns Assyria's own cruelty back on its king. The hunter becomes the hunted, the leash-holder becomes the one on the leash.

**Verse 35 — The overnight devastation:** The narrator tells it in one verse. One hundred and eighty-five thousand soldiers, dead by morning. No battle scene. No heroic combat. Just dawn and corpses. The understatement is more terrifying than any description of divine warfare could be.

*— PNEUMA*
